items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: I always did like a lot of attack. I've always liked that -- that's what I got from Bix Beiderbecke.

ctx.x: Those guys were great trumpet players. And you see you get a little something from everybody that just automatically you just -- you just -- I guess absorb a lot of things, a lot of styles into -- and before you know it, you have a style of your own. That comes -- that comes -- I always did like a lot of attack. I've always liked that -- that's what I got from Bix Beiderbecke. I think Bix Beiderbecke had the greatest attack for playing jazz of any trumpet player.

Now don't -- Louie didn't have all that attack, he didn't need it, he didn't want it, because he was a different approach and Bix had an attack, that I liked and I think I still have that attack. Cause I like it because it -- it -- immediately attracts attention, you know, I do it every night a lot of times before I blast last night I played it all night long -- an attack like that and people turn around and everybody coming up there. You know? It's important. And I think if you're doing something, do it so…
